newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SAYS PROFITS TO "NORMALISE" IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SAYS PROFITS TO "NORMALISE" IN 1997.

text.p: Philips Electronics said on Thursday it was confident its 1997 results would regain customary levels.
The company earlier reported that bottom-line 1996 net results plunged to a 590 million guilder loss from a year-earlier net profit of 2.52 billion, smashed by hefty restructuring provisions.
"We are confident we will produce a result in 1997 in line with normal expectations," Philips chairman Cor Boonstra told a news conference.
It was this confidence that underlay Philips' decision to hold its dividend steady at 1.60 guilders per share despite the sharply lower 1996 results, Boonstra said.
Pressed to give an indication of "normal expectations", Boonstra declined to name any figures beyond repeating his target of double-digit growth in income from operations.
"You should be looking at the IFO (income from operations) line in our performance," he told journalists.
Philips earlier reported fourth-quarter income from operations fell to 288 million guilders from a year-earlier 1.26 billion guilders.
Over the full year, income from operations more than halved to 1.81 billion guilders from 4.04 billion guilders in 1995.
- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +3120 504 5000.
